title: Real conversations
goal: Ask for help, react and give opinions, link ideas, and visit and say goodbye politely.

notes.p: {{咗|zo2}} shows the change has already happened: {{唔見咗|m4 gin3 zo2}} = gone missing, {{壞咗|waai6 zo2}} = broken, {{蕩失咗路|dong6 sat1 zo2 lou6}} = lost my way. {{有啲|jau5 di1}} before something unpleasant = a bit: {{有啲唔舒服|jau5 di1 m4 syu1 fuk6}}. To ask for help: {{你可唔可以幫我呀？|nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 aa3}} or {{唔該幫我|m4 goi1 bong1 ngo5}} + what you need. Phones are counted with {{部|bou6}}.
ex: ngo5 m4 gin3 zo2 go3 ngan4 baau1
ngo5 bou6 sau2 gei1 mou5 din6
ngo5 jau5 di1 m4 syu1 fuk6
ngo5 wan2 m4 dou2 dei6 tit3 zaam6
I can't find the MTR station.

notes.p: {{係囉|hai6 lo1}} = exactly, that's what I'm saying; {{囉|lo1}} marks something obvious. {{唔係嘛|m4 hai6 maa3}} = no way, you're kidding. {{真係？|zan1 hai6}} = really? {{梗係啦|gang2 hai6 laa1}} = of course. {{我都係|ngo5 dou1 hai6}} = me too. Tone trap: {{嘛|maa3}} in {{唔係嘛|m4 hai6 maa3}} is mid and level; {{媽|maa1}} (mom) is high.

{{雖然|seoi1 jin4}} … {{但係|daan6 hai6}} … = although …, … Cantonese keeps both words, where English drops the "but". {{不過|bat1 gwo3}} is a softer "but". {{仲|zung6}} = still; {{仲未|zung6 mei6}} = still not. {{已經|ji5 ging1}} = already, usually with {{咗|zo2}}. {{即係|zik1 hai6}} = that means, in other words.
ex: seoi1 jin4 hou2 gwai3, daan6 hai6 hou2 hou2 sik6
hou2 zeng3, bat1 gwo3 hou2 do1 jan4

notes.p: At the start of a sentence, {{咁|gam2}} (rising tone) = so, well then. It is also in {{咁諗|gam2 nam2}} = think so. Before a describing word, as in level 9, it is {{咁|gam3}} (mid level tone) = so, as: {{冇咁貴|mou5 gam3 gwai3}}. Listen for the tone to tell them apart.
ex: ni1 go3 mou5 go2 go3 gam3 gwai3
This one isn't as expensive as that one.

notes.p: The host says {{歡迎|fun1 jing4}}, {{入嚟坐啦|jap6 lai4 co5 laa1}} and {{隨便坐|ceoi4 bin2 co5}}. When someone thanks you, say {{唔使客氣|m4 sai2 haak3 hei3}}. A guest leaving says {{我走先喇|ngo5 zau2 sin1 laa3}} and {{打擾晒|daa2 jiu2 saai3}}; the host answers {{慢慢行|maan6 maan2 haang4}}. For a longer goodbye: {{保重|bou2 zung6}}, or {{一路順風|jat1 lou6 seon6 fung1}} for someone travelling.
ex: maan6 maan2 haang4, haa6 ci3 zoi3 lai4 laa1
Take care, come again next time.

q: ngo5 m4 gin3 ___ go3 ngan4 baau1
items.why: {{唔見咗|m4 gin3 zo2}} = has gone missing; {{咗|zo2}} shows it already happened.
{{壞咗|waai6 zo2}} = has broken, so it's broken now.

q: seoi1 jin4 hou2 gwai3, ___ hou2 hou2 sik6
items.why: {{雖然|seoi1 jin4}} pairs with {{但係|daan6 hai6}}; Cantonese keeps both.

q: ___ lok6 gan2 jyu5, daan6 hai6 ngo5 dei6 dou1 soeng2 heoi3
items.en: Although it's raining, we still want to go.
items.why: {{但係|daan6 hai6}} in the second half needs {{雖然|seoi1 jin4}} in the first.
{{已經|ji5 ging1}} = already, together with {{咗|zo2}}.
{{仲未|zung6 mei6}} = still not.

items.en: You're welcome. (No need to be polite.)
items.why: {{唔使|m4 sai2}} = no need to. {{唔要|m4 jiu3}} means "don't want".
{{即係|zik1 hai6}} = that means; {{即係點呀？|zik1 hai6 dim2 aa3}} = meaning what?
{{囉|lo1}} marks something obvious: {{係囉|hai6 lo1}} = exactly.
{{唔係嘛|m4 hai6 maa3}} shows surprise or disbelief.

items.en: (Host to guest) Come in and sit down.
items.why: {{入嚟|jap6 lai4}} = come in: {{嚟|lai4}} means towards the speaker.

items.en: (Leaving a friend's home) Thanks for having me!
items.why: {{打擾晒|daa2 jiu2 saai3}} is the fixed phrase; {{晒|saai3}} = all, completely.
{{我走先喇|ngo5 zau2 sin1 laa3}}: {{先|sin1}} goes after the verb.

items.why: {{保重|bou2 zung6}} = take care of yourself, for a longer goodbye.

items.why: {{唔該借借|m4 goi1 ze3 ze3}} = excuse me, let me through.

items.q: Your friend says the queue is too long. You were just thinking the same thing. You say:
items.why: {{係囉|hai6 lo1}} = exactly, that's what I'm saying.

items.why: {{唔係嘛|m4 hai6 maa3}} = no way! (surprise).

roleplay.title: Dinner at a friend's flat
roleplay.setup: Your Hong Kong friend Wing has invited you to his flat for dinner. Arrive, be a good guest, chat about Hong Kong, and leave politely.
roleplay.persona: You are Wing, a friendly Hong Konger hosting the learner at your flat in Sha Tin. Welcome them, tell them to come in and sit anywhere, say there is no need to take off their shoes, and offer tea. Ask what they think of Hong Kong and react naturally with 係囉, 唔係嘛, 梗係啦 or 真係？. When they leave, say 慢慢行 and invite them back. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, using mostly words from levels 1 to 10.
opening: fun1 jing4 fun1 jing4! jap6 lai4 co5 laa1
roleplay.opening_en: Welcome, welcome! Come in and sit down.
goals: Thank your host and compliment the home
Give an opinion about Hong Kong using 'although … but …'
React to something your host says with surprise or agreement
Leave politely and thank your host for having you

roleplay.title: Lost in Causeway Bay
roleplay.setup: You're in Causeway Bay. Your phone is dead and you can't find the MTR station. Ask a passer-by for help.
roleplay.persona: You are a kind middle-aged woman (an auntie) on a street in Causeway Bay. The MTR station is two minutes away: go straight, then turn right at the second street. Notice the learner looks lost, ask if they are lost, give simple directions, and offer to let them use your phone if they ask. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, using mostly words from levels 1 to 10. End warmly with 唔使客氣 and 小心啲.
opening: nei5 hai6 mai6 dong6 sat1 zo2 lou6 aa3
goals: Explain that you're lost and your phone is dead
Ask how to get to the MTR station
Ask her to help you with something
